evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂說明; historical variant relationship and cited attestations
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies 㝡 as a nonstandard/later variant of 最, citing a Sui Longzangsi stele and references that describe this spelling in Six Dynasties usage. It quotes Guangyun’s gloss 最，極也 (“utmost”) and notes 㝡 as a common form in that period. This supports 最 → later 㝡 as a variant relationship, not 㝡 as the original form of 最.
evidence.title: [A00302-005] (最) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Multi-function Dictionary), character entry 最
evidence.field: 《說文》; form records; 形義通解; cited classical examples
evidence.text: The entry repeats Shuowen’s 「犯而取也。从冃从取」 (“to offend/force one’s way and take”), records Guangyun fanqie 祖外 and Middle Chinese category 精母、泰韻、合口一等, and displays a seal-script form. Its visible table has no bronze or oracle forms. It separately cites 最 in Han shu as an administrative ranking term, Yan Danzi as a foremost person or thing, Xiao erya for 要 (“summary/essential”), Guan Zi for 聚 (“gather,” in a commentator’s gloss), Shi ji for a total, and Mozi for “foremost”; the entry gives no comprehensive first-attestation chronology for these senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Multi-function Dictionary), character entry 取
evidence.field: form history and independent lexical use
evidence.text: The dossier’s inspected entry reports oracle and bronze forms of 取 as 耳 plus 又, interpreted as a hand holding an ear, and gives early uses in the sense “obtain/take.” That establishes an independent history for the graph and word 取, but does not decide whether 取 functions semantically or phonetically in 最.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, versioned Old Chinese reconstruction table
evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese rows for 最 and 取; table search result opened
evidence.text: The table lists 最 as Mandarin zuì, Middle Chinese tswajH, Old Chinese *[ts]ˤot-s, gloss “collect; most.” It lists 取 with multiple readings: qǔ, tshjuX, *tsʰoʔ “take”; cǒu, tshuwX, *tsʰˤoʔ “take”; and qù, tshjuH, *[ts]ʰoʔ-s “take (a wife).” Within this reconstruction system, these rows support a broad rhyme/ending resemblance, but differ in initial and conditioning; this comparison alone cannot establish 取 as the phonetic component of 最. The actual local rows checked were `/home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-dict/sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv`: 最 has the same listed row and 取 has those three rows. The PDF opened unsuccessfully, so the local exact rows are recorded as local checks, while the inspected versioned table search output verifies the displayed forms.
evidence.kind: reconstruction table plus local exact-row cross-check
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

gaps: The accessible sources do not establish a pre-Han original graphic form for 最, a graphic sequence from an original 㝡 form, or a theory that distinguishing marks were added later. The Ministry of Education page lists early-form resources for 最 as unpublished; the inspected character entry supplies a seal form only.

The traditional Shuowen account parses 冃 + 取 as a meaning-based phrase (“offend/force one’s way and take”). Other dossier sources propose a phonosemantic analysis with 取 as sound. No inspected primary paleographic evidence resolves these competing analyses. Similarities in Baxter–Sagart reconstructions are relevant comparison data, not proof of phonetic function.

The proposed explanation that a whole 取 graph was borrowed for 最’s superlative meaning is not demonstrated. Evidence for 取’s independent “take” word and graph does not itself establish whole-graph borrowing.

Cited sources give examples of different senses but no securely ordered first attestations for the modern superlative “most,” “extremely,” “gather,” ranking, summary, or total. Semantic links among those uses remain undemonstrated; dictionary gloss order is not chronology.

Official Unihan per-character endpoints for 最 and 取 could not be opened. The exact current kMandarin readings are preserved from local rows, while Unicode’s general lookup interface is cited only for the kind of data its database supplies.

Commons glyphs are digital redrawings in Shuowen seal-script style rather than artifact photographs. The 最 SVG has explicit Sinica source and CC0 statement. For 取, the exact file page and original link were inspected; its available provenance is less specific. No separate Xiaoxuetang candidate was selected because the query endpoint did not open.
